title: QUIC RFC 9000 Packet Classification And Connection Association
purpose: Describe the bounded endpoint ingress floor that classifies packets, associates routed packets with existing connections, supports server Initial admission, and handles zero-length connection-ID routing.
design_summary: The endpoint ingress path classifies datagrams by header form before routing. Long-header packets route by exact Destination Connection ID after excluding Version Negotiation and Retry endpoint-handled packets. Short-header packets route by the longest registered Destination Connection ID prefix, including the zero-length route when a connection has selected zero-length connection-ID mode. The zero-length route is intentionally scoped to the local endpoint tuple so remote address or port changes can still be processed while traffic for a different local endpoint is not associated. Listener-host pre-acceptance remains responsible for creating a new server connection from a conforming Initial packet when no existing route matches.
data_and_state_considerations: Routes live in QuicConnectionRuntimeEndpoint buckets keyed by connection-ID length and route key. Zero-length routes rely on endpoint binding state rather than peer connection-ID bytes. Routed packets are posted to the owning runtime as QuicConnectionPacketReceivedEvent instances; malformed or unroutable packets do not reach the runtime path.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Maximum-length connection IDs route through the same exact-match path as ordinary non-zero connection IDs.
Zero-length connection-ID routing can match across remote address changes when the local endpoint remains stable.
Packets with different protocol versions and endpoint-handled weakly protected packet forms remain discardable before runtime processing.
The weak-protection rollback tail is not closed by this design.
risks: Later work still needs focused proof for packet-protection removal failure and rollback after weakly protected packet processing discovers an error.
Future endpoint routing changes must preserve the distinction between existing-connection association and listener pre-acceptance admission.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes only the packet classification, connection association, zero-length route matching, version mismatch discard, and weakly protected invalid packet discard floor. It does not claim packet-protection removal failure handling, pre-error connection-error generation, rollback of weakly protected packet side effects, public API widening, or hosted interop readiness.
